title: A Rolling Window GARCH Analysis to Measure the Change in Efficiency of the Johannesburg Stock Exchange
content: The efficiency of a stock exchange has many implications, including the likely effectiveness of active investing and the accurate pricing of assets. The Johannesburg Stock Exchange has been found to be efficient in prior research, but there is recent evidence that its efficiency is declining. The study aimed to determine whether the efficiency of the exchange has declined, as proxied by the speed of mean reversion of returns, and whether any change was specifically driven by smaller stocks as we know that large stocks are efficiently priced on the exchange. A general autoregressive conditional heteroskedasticity (1,1) was applied to the data together with an Augmented Dickey Fuller based test for robustness. The results show a decline in efficiency of the stock exchange as well as for the different sub-indices studied. All sub-indices studied declined in efficiency, but this is not ascribed to smaller listed firms, but rather an overall decline in the efficiency of the stock exchange. A recommendation is made for a future study to consider the speed of reversion of individual stocks which would allow the study of firm characteristics possibly driving the change in efficiency of the exchange.
